blocks.text: Two distinct questions affect how this chapter is read. John 8:1-11 has a long history of being received as Scripture, yet it is absent from the earliest major Greek witnesses and appears in different locations in later copies; many therefore judge it not to have belonged to John’s earliest recoverable form. Later in the chapter, Jesus’ repeated “I am” sayings work in more than one way: some are ordinary identification, while others carry symbolic or wider claims. Each saying should be read in its own immediate setting rather than treated as though they all mean precisely the same thing.
